questions: Does the five-sensor array at 12 mm pitch give a usable, non-saturated signal, or do readings sit at 0 or 1 too often?
Is the 0.12 m wheel track or 0.03 m radius limiting turn rate or top speed?
Is the 50 mm forward sensor offset useful, or does it cause lag on tight bends?
Which track, if any, forces the robot off the line, and at what point?

intent: Baseline geometry for the first race: a symmetric five-sensor front array at 12 mm pitch matched to the 12 mm footprint, forward of the axle to give lead time on bends, with a light, compact body to favour acceleration and quick turn response. The intent is to establish whether this platform can complete the oval, s-bend and slalom within 3 s without line loss. The Integrator should report how the array reads on each track, especially whether the outer sensors ever see the line and whether the wheels or body limit steering.
learning: Baseline with no prior race evidence. Next iteration, use the measured rms_error, max_error and line_loss_events to decide whether to widen the sensor spread or move sensors forward or back, and use completion_time to decide whether to change wheel radius or mass to gain speed.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or integration feedback, so this is a baseline built from the contract rather than from evidence. Five sensors spaced 12 mm apart, matching the 12 mm footprint, give continuous coverage of the 25 mm tape with no gaps, and the outermost pair sits at +/-24 mm so a line offset of roughly 3 cm is still seen. Sensors sit 50 mm ahead of the axle so the robot reads the line before it reaches the wheels. The wheel track is 0.12 m and the wheel radius 0.03 m, a middle-of-range drivetrain that should allow the speed needed for a sub-3 s finish. Mass is 0.6 kg, low in range, to reduce inertia and help acceleration and turn response. Body width 0.14 m keeps the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.035) = 0.06, so the body does not widen the allowed error. Body length 0.16 m is mid-range; it only affects yaw inertia, which is low at this mass. I expect a completed run on the oval and s-bend with few line losses, with the slalom as the hardest case. I have not tested this, so the next race will show whether the sensor coverage and the speed budget hold.
